Ballentine v. Hall, No. 1:26-cv-02331 — Rule 26(f) Conference and Proposed Judicial
Subject:
Counsel:
On October 16, 2026, I initiated the Rule 26(f) conference process in writing and requested a response
by October 30, 2026. As of today, October 28, I have received no response from Meta.
Rule 26(f)(2) places responsibility for arranging and participating in the conference on the parties
collectively. I remain prepared to conduct the conference and develop the required discovery plan.
Prior correspondence raised the prospect of a motion to stay discovery upon initiation of the Rule 26(f)
process. No such motion has been filed, and no order staying the parties' Rule 26(f) obligations has been
I write to ascertain Meta's position and determine whether judicial intervention is necessary.
Specifically:
1. Participation: Does Meta intend to participate in the Rule 26(f) conference?
2. Basis for nonparticipation: Does Meta contend that any existing order or other authority
excuses or postpones its Rule 26(f) obligations? If so, please identify that authority.
3. Proposed judicial relief: Would Meta oppose an order directing the parties to conduct the
Rule 26(f) conference by a date certain and submit a discovery plan identifying any unresolved
disagreements? If so, on what grounds?
The October 30 response deadline established in my original correspondence remains unchanged. My
objective is to determine whether the parties can fulfill their obligations without requiring the Court's
intervention.
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
